newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan bourse ends September slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan bourse ends September slightly lower.

text.p: The Casablanca bourse on Monday ended slightly lower, pulled down by the market's biggest companies, including Societe Nationale d'Investissement, traders said.
The bourse all-share index dropped 0.20 percent to close at 427.73 points.

"After weeks of a continuous upper trend partly triggered by the expected introduction of the Moroccan bourse in the IFC (World Bank's International Finance Corp) emerging market index, the market recorded a slight fall," said Mohamed Mekouar, analyst at Upline Securities.
"However the bourse index is expected to resume its upward trend after the listed stocks published their half-year positive results," Mekouar said.
The U.S.-based IFC is expected to unveil on Tuesday the names of a dozen Moroccan companies whose closing prices will be regulary monitored.

SNI, which controls stakes in more than 40 companies and has a capitalisation of 5.8 billion dirhans, lost five dirhams. Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur, one of the market blue chips, lost three to close at 402 dirhams.
Samir refinery, Morocco's main oil plant and in which the government expects to sell a stake of up to 51 percent to foreign oil investors, dropped two to 250 dirhams.

Banque Commerciale du Maroc, the market largest capitalisation, remained unchanged at 670 dirhams. The traded volume on the official market dropped to 19.2 million dirhams from 45.8 million dirhams on Friday, stockbrokers said.
